title: HomeFlow: A Data Flywheel for Smart Home Agent Training with Verifiable Simulation
claim: A closed-loop data flywheel turns simulated environments and intents into verified trajectories that train a stronger agent.
layout: 3 stacked rows, left-to-right flow, MCTS tree in middle row
description: A dense three-tier diagram of the whole system. The top row has two boxed modules joined by an arrow and an LLM node. On the left, the simulation environment (HomeMaker) shows household information: a room floor plan, smart devices, and indoor and outdoor scenes. On the right, Blueprint Construction shows a person on a sofa (situation, feeling, intent) and green-checked state conditions such as light brightness and colour temperature. The middle row, under an orange banner reading Dialogue Synthesis with MCTSFlow, has four panels: a user-agent dialogue example, a tree expansion with user and agent nodes and green or red terminal checks, HomeEnv verification, and trajectory selection by shortest or best path. The bottom row shows data pools M1, M2 and M3 feeding SFT cold start, single-turn and multi-turn RL, online RL, and an improved policy. Orange, blue and green accents; the eye starts at the top-left and follows the arrows downward.
caption: Overview of HomeFlow. Based on HomeEnv, HomeMaker generates diverse home environments. Blueprint then creates executable scene conditions, followed by MCTS-Flow to synthesize diverse, verifiable trajectories. From this architecture, we derive three data synthesis strategies: (M1) pure-text role-play (w/o Blueprint); (M2) Blueprint-grounded linear generation (w/o MCTS-Flow); and (M3) the complete HomeFlow pipeline.
abstract: Large language model agents are moving beyond text-only interaction toward physical-world control, with smart homes as a representative domain. Real domestic interaction requires understanding ambiguous intents, operating in dynamic environments, and performing multi-turn reasoning. However, existing methods struggle to generate high-quality training data for smart home agents. We propose HomeFlow, a verifiable data flywheel for this domain. HomeFlow uses HomeEnv as a unified simulation environment and HomeMaker to procedurally generate diverse home settings. Subsequently, Blueprint compiles open-ended user intents into executable state-based success conditions, while MCTS-Flow synthesizes diverse, verifiable multi-turn trajectories through environment-guided tree search. We then optimize the agents via supervised fine-tuning and step-wise RLVE, which facilitates iterative improvement through authentic physical feedback. We further construct SmartHome-Bench to evaluate the agent across various smart home tasks. On this benchmark, HomeFlow-RL-4B and HomeFlow-RL-8B achieve task success rates of 84.60% and 87.03%. It is worth noting that HomeFlow-RL-8B even surpasses the leading GPT-5.5 by 1.23 percentage points.
